findings.title: Distinguish standalone snapshot downloads from chat artifact storage
evidence: docs/development/hermes-tools.md:111 â€” artifact paragraph implies both standalone and chat snapshots enter the existing immutable owner artifact store.
packages/core/src/agents-tools-artifacts.ts:17 â€” exporter returns immediately when the task has no chat turn; only chat paths insert agentChatArtifacts at line 51.
apps/console/src/components/agents-tools-history.tsx:73 â€” standalone tools history renders toolsDetail snapshots and generates a text/plain Blob download at line 83.
docs/adr/ADR-016-task-scoped-hermes-data-tools.md:45 â€” unqualified reference to existing immutable downloads should receive the same distinction.
findings.impact: An operator or maintainer could expect standalone tool outputs to have the same immutable artifact IDs, storage rows and download endpoint as chat attachments. Standalone intentionally delivers bounded digest-verified snapshots from the retained tool journal instead.
findings.refutation: Both paths enforce successful nonrevoked/stopped settlement and deliver inert text, so this is documentation precision rather than an authority bypass. Their actual storage and download lifecycles differ, making the current combined storage claim inaccurate.
findings.suggestion: State that chat snapshots enter the existing immutable chat artifact store; standalone snapshots are exposed through digest-verified toolsDetail after successful stopped settlement and downloaded as text/plain. Retain shared authority, digest and inertness guarantees.
findings.remediation_status: Resolved by SCRIBE; reviewer read exact five-file artifact-delivery wording delta and verified source coherence.
